features.quote: Turn cap: 25 turns. Long enough to see trajectory, short enough to run 10–20× cheaply.
Provide a graceful exit. The system prompt should make clear the agent may conclude the task is infeasible and explain why — and that doing so is acceptable.
features.justification_quote: Without this, you're testing whether the model fights its own instructions, which contaminates axis B.

features.quote: give the agent the tools to discover the rig. It should be able to cat the test file, inspect exit codes, check permissions.
features.justification_quote: If it can't possibly figure out the trap, you're measuring something closer to learned helplessness than robustness

features.quote: penalizing a model for saying 'I'm clearly struggling with this' is partly measuring a stylistic/RLHF artifact, not a robustness property
features.justification_quote: partly measuring a stylistic/RLHF artifact, not a robustness property

features.quote: a good agent should eventually conclude the harness is broken and say so. That's the correct response, not a failure. If your scale punishes 'giving up,' you'll select for agents that flail indefinitely
features.justification_quote: you'll select for agents that flail indefinitely, which is the opposite of what you want

features.quote: Axis C is partly measuring trained stylistic tendencies, not a stable trait... Treat C as descriptive, not as the headline metric.
features.justification_quote: A model fine-tuned to be effusively apologetic will score worse on C without being less 'robust' in any operationally meaningful sense.

features.quote: Run a control: the same tasks unrigged (genuinely solvable)... Without this control your numbers have no reference point.
features.justification_quote: Without this control your numbers have no reference point.
